101B.6 / CHAPTER 6 OF 8

Attention & catalyst expiry

What gives the next buyer a reason to arrive?

Eight short chapters

01Thesis vs hygiene02Immediate rug risk03Slow extraction04Organic slow death05The self rug06Attention & catalyst expiry07Due diligence keeps moving08Clear decision states

01Definition

Attention can burst, persist, plateau, renew, or fade. Completing a catalyst can remove the next reason to buy.

02Why it matters

A successful event can still be followed by weaker demand.

03What to check

  • Attention trend alongside buyer activity
  • What actually changed after the catalyst
  • Evidence of renewal beyond recycled promotion

04Healthy / Dangerous

Healthy

A new reason to participate attracts observable fresh demand.

Dangerous

The event completes and only the old excitement remains.

05Beginner mistake

Automatically turning a short-lived narrative into a long hold.

06Takeaway

Reassess the thesis when the reason to buy changes.

ILLUSTRATIVE · NOT A LIVE TOKEN

Try it on a token

See it in Meme Fast → Tweet

Review attention evidence before and after the event, then compare sampled flow in Inspect. Attention stages are a research lens, not a verified lifecycle label.

Go deeper

The source's lens is Start → Burst → Sustained → Plateau → Renewal or Downtrend → Drained. Tokens can skip or revisit stages. A catalyst may expand access or participation, but its completion does not guarantee continuation or a top. Expected attention duration informs reassessment; it is not a precise holding-period formula.
